ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As illustrated in the diagram, two strips with a width of 2 and parallel opposite edges are placed crosswise on top of each other. By rotating one of the strips, we obtain a quadrilateral ABCD, where $\angle ABC=60^\circ$. What is the area of the quadrilateral ABCD?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw CF$\perp$AB at point F, and draw AE$\perp$BC at point E through point A.\\
According to the problem, we know: AE=CF=2,\\
$\because$ $\angle$ABC=60$^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$FCB=30$^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ let BF=x, then BC=2x,\\
$\therefore$ $4x^{2}-x^{2}=4$,\\
$\therefore$ x=$\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}$,\\
$\therefore$ BC=$\frac{4\sqrt{3}}{3}$,\\
$\because$ AB$\parallel$CD, AD$\parallel$BC,\\
$\therefore$ Quadrilateral ABCD is a parallelogram,\\
$\therefore$ $S_{\square ABCD}$=BC·AE=$\frac{4\sqrt{3}}{3} \times 2=\boxed{\frac{8\sqrt{3}}{3}}$.
